lines.t: Three curtains, three pages, one tale. Now it's yours to tell. Tell it badly at first — everyone does.
You passed all three curtains of dusk? Then you've read the whole tale: the kin who hid the last song in the shadows.
My grandmother told it to me under this very willow. Take these. A story that's finished ought to pay its listener.
Three curtains of dusk. One hangs here in the fen, by the sinkhole west of my willow.
One in the Undertone, on the far west wall of the lower galleries. One in a Galewick cellar. Shade voices part them.
Ah — a Veil-tuned Keynote. Then you can part the curtains of dusk. Most folk walk straight past them.
Behind each hangs a page of an old tale. Bring me all three and I'll tell you how it ends. Well?
Hear the frogs? They sing in thirds when the stone's awake. The fen had forgotten its own tune for a week.
There are curtains of dusk in this land, you know. Shadows you can walk behind. Come back when shade answers you.
Sit, sit. The fog brings out the old stories. This one's about curtains of dusk — shadows that hide a door.
…But I can't tell it with that bell-fitting racket at the stone. Whispering woman, clipboards. Spoils the mood.
Your loud friend in the scarf went east grinning. Sillowmere's that way — the Mere Hall sits on piles in the middle.
Hear that? The fen's got its voice back. You can feel it in the boardwalk — toxin kin fight with a spring in their step now.
Some kid in a red scarf is waiting at the boardwalk end, east. Looked lost. Said they weren't. Looked more lost.
You saw off the whispering woman! The bell's off the stone, then. Go and give it a hum — any kin will do.
Keep to the boardwalks. The pools bubble violet, but it's only the fen breathing. Mostly.
Engineers are at the half-sunk stone, fitting a brass bell over it. Since they came, even the frogs have gone quiet.
You're standing in a marked service area. I'm obliged to remove you. Politely.
I'll have to file an incident report. It's three pages. The Warden will want to read it aloud. With feeling.
The Magister says unregulated stones are how people get hurt. She's usually right about hazards.
*Enter the hero, stage left, too loud as usual.*
This stone is being fitted for a Stillbell, darling. Do sit down.
*Exit, pursued by a Tuner.* How very dramatic of you.
A Stillbell doesn't hurt a stone. It simply decides *when*. Isn't that what a conductor does?
Vey's crew unclamp the trial Stillbell and haul it off through the reeds. The half-sunk stone is left bare and silent.
{starter} pads up to the stone and hums. For a moment, nothing. Then the stone answers, low and warm.
Colour ripples out across Sallowfen. The frogs start up all at once, in thirds.
*Intermission.* Go on, then. Fix your little stone. I'll be reviewing you harshly.
{starter} pads up to the half-sunk stone and hums. The stone answers, low and warm, and colour ripples across the fen.
A Stillbell doesn't hurt a stone. It simply decides *when*. Isn't that what a conductor does?
{player}! There you are. I was going to help with the stone. I got lost. The frogs all look the same.
Battle me so I feel competent.
You fixed a *stone*. I was busy losing to a frog. Don't tell anyone.
…Do you ever feel like everyone's already decided who you are?
Never mind. Forget it. Sillowmere's east — race you. I'll lose that too, probably. Go on.
*Enter the hero, stage left, too loud as usual.* This stone is being fitted for a Stillbell, darling. Do sit down.
*Exit, pursued by a Tuner.* How very dramatic of you.
*Blackout.* Go home, little critic.
A Stillbell doesn't hurt a stone. It simply decides *when*. Isn't that what a conductor does?
I was going to help with the stone. I got lost. The frogs all look the same. Battle me so I feel competent.
You fixed a *stone*. I was busy losing to a frog. Don't tell anyone.
Okay, that helped. I feel fully competent. Frogs, beware.
